fixes.was: Congress may by statute withdraw a court's jurisdiction so completely that its later actions are void and open to collateral attack, even if the affected party never contested jurisdiction or appealed in that court.
fixes.now: Under its bankruptcy power, Congress may by a specific statute withdraw another court's power to proceed against a protected debtor, so that its later actions are void and open to collateral attack even if the debtor never contested jurisdiction or appealed there.

fixes.was: The court distinguished a voluntary governmental intention from an enforceable right, which the Commission could not compel Eritrea to honor.
fixes.now: The court distinguished a voluntary governmental intention from an enforceable right; the Commission could not compel Eritrea to honor that intention.
